electrification_type.applicability: Exactly Unlimited Sport Altitude, US MY2019 Wrangler JL ERC offering, candidate digest sha256:7de133eb5646f2832af03106bcd6396cd5e189a89fa1f00556d3713806ebddcf; inherited body/model-code and engine-offering lineage remains in the pinned candidate. No ERG/eTorque, EC3, other model year, or tuning identity is classified.
electrification_type.limitations: No explicit US ERC naturally aspirated/nonhybrid statement was found. Australian-to-US induction continuity and the ERC conventional-hardware association are derived. Catalog provenance and MY2020 introduction chronology are not conclusive alone. Regulatory material and retrospective FCA Y40 also describe MY2019 3.6L hybrid/eTorque applications without establishing that they are ERC; the proposal is restricted to the ten retained ERC offerings, not all MY2019 3.6L Wranglers.
electrification_type.reasoning: Propose none for the ten offered ERC configurations. US manual hardware descriptions distinguish conventional ESS starting equipment from an eTorque motor-generator with hybrid battery and launch assistance; the MY2019 catalog positively identifies conventional without-eTorque alternator applications and a separate ERG BSG application. US offering lineage binds the ten rows to ERC ESS; contemporary MY2020 powertrain materials separately introduce/describe V6 eTorque Sahara. The combined architecture/applicability judgment requires human adjudication; neither ESS terminology, missing eTorque words nor introduction chronology alone establishes nonhybrid status.

The MY19 technical guide positively classifies the same marketed family/ESS architecture as naturally aspirated; applicable US guide/specification lineage identifies ERC, its marketed dimensions and trim/body offerings.
